title: refactor(ci): simplify lint/test workflows, improve cache parallelism and release automation
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: our current GitHub Actions matrix for lint/test/release has grown organically and suffers from slow builds, duplicated job setup, and cache contention that increases CI queue time. This PR consolidates workflows across the monorepo to a smaller set of shared actions, improves cache key strategy and parallelism for node package caches, and centralizes release automation steps. Goals: 1) Reduce CI wall-clock time for common PRs (lint + unit test) by ~25-40%. 2) Reduce duplicate workflow maintenance across SDK and examples repos. 3) Make release job idempotent and faster with a deterministic cache and explicit artifact verification. Changeset summary: - Introduced .github/workflows/ci-common.yml with reusable jobs for setup, restore-cache, install, and test runners. - Refactored per-repo workflow files to call the reusable jobs (lint.yml, test.yml, integration.yml). - Updated cache keys to include node-version, lockfile checksum, and package-ecosystem fingerprint to reduce cross-job misses. - Added parallelism config for cache restore/restore-keys to allow N concurrent cache fetches (controlled via workflow input, default 4). - Consolidated release automation into tools/release/release.yml with a dry-run mode and improved artifact checksum checks. - Minor package.json devDependency bumps for @actions/core and @actions/cache to address flaky cache pruning. Checklist: - [x] Move shared steps into reusable workflows - [x] Update SDKs and examples to call new jobs - [x] Add cache key fingerprinting and parallelism knobs - [x] Validate release dry-run - [x] Run full monorepo CI and fix breakages Observability & metrics: added workflow duration annotations and a metric emission hook (tools/ci/emit_metrics.sh) to track job-level timings and cache hit rates. Related: ENG-4821 (CI perf), ENG-4910 (release automation hygiene), SUP-1234 (customer-facing build flakiness incident). Notes: kept changes minimal in runtime code; most edits are CI config and helper scripts. If problems appear, revert by reverting the head branch or toggling workflow usage via feature flag in .github/workflows/ci-common.yml.
